complexity_ledger.justification: No representation added and none needed. MF-030 is a scripts-only change to the complexity analyzer -- it makes `analyze complexity` follow EXTENDS and union declarations across the module hierarchy, and fail closed on constructs it cannot model (INSTANCE, WITH substitution, parameterized instantiation, LOCAL, unresolved EXTENDS). The bound is UNCHANGED for every single-file spec, because such specs extend only standard library modules and resolution is a no-op: TlaSpecDevCli.tla still resolves to 9 variables and bound 699,840, and TLC re-measured 231,621 distinct / depth 25. Zero delta is the required outcome: max_state_space_bound is at 70% and MF-019 proved a single boolean breaches it, so the owner forbade adding model state. The correction the ticket makes is to the MEASUREMENT of decomposed models, not to any model.

gate_violations: component C1 is touched by 14 actions, exceeding max_component_actions 8

complexity_ledger.narrative: MF-030 closes a silent failure of the epic's binding complexity gate. analyze_complexity.py read one .tla file and stopped at EXTENDS, so on the decomposed architecture SKILL.md mandates it scored only the declarations literally present in the analyzed file. The error is never conservative: missing variables only ever shrink the product bound, so the gate failed toward PASS on exactly the shape the skill requires. MF-023 measured External reporting bound = 1 over 2 of 9 variables from this. The fix is a partial module resolver (resolve_module) that follows EXTENDS through the hierarchy and unions VARIABLES, CONSTANTS, and the top-level definitions carrying TypeInvariant/Init/actions, base-first with the extending module overriding inherited names. Standard TLA+ library modules (Naturals, Integers, Reals, Sequences, FiniteSets, Bags, TLC, Json) declare no VARIABLES the bound reads and are skipped rather than resolved to a file. Every construct the resolver cannot model FAILS CLOSED with a named error rather than under-reporting: INSTANCE / named and unnamed instantiation, WITH substitution, and parameterized instantiation via UnsupportedModuleConstructError; LOCAL via the same; and an EXTENDS naming a non-standard module with no findable .tla via UnresolvedExtendsError. analyze() propagates these; run() and gate_report() catch them and fail closed (nonzero / gate FAIL with the reason). This honours references/architecture_tractability.md "No Degenerate Escapes": when a model cannot be resolved, write the failure, not a smaller number. Measured alternatives and the self-scrutiny check: the risk flagged for this ticket was a resolver that appears to work on a model where the extended declarations do not matter to the bound. The regression fixture is deliberately the opposite -- Channel EXTENDS Counter, where the EXTENDED module carries the only bound-bearing variable (tick in 0..3) and the extending module adds only an unconstrained channel variable. Pre-fix the analyzer reports variables= ['emitted'], bound=1, Bump absent; post-fix variables={tick,emitted}, bound=4, Bump present. The number moves 1->4 and the assertions were run against the HEAD analyzer to confirm they fail pre-fix. Shipped example re-measured (examples/distributed_history, External EXTENDS Internal EXTENDS Core, no TypeInvariant so bound is 1 both ways): its verdict stays FAIL but the diagnosis is corrected from a spurious "C2 {responses} touched by 9 actions" (an artifact of seeing only External's 4 variables) to the true "C1 {accounts,carts,orders, responses} touched by 13 actions" over all 10 variables, with named port-crossing actions and modularity 0.000 -> 0.230. That corrected figure is relevant to MF-037 and the ticket-workflow example: any downstream copy of the old 9-action number is stale. Evidence: results/tlc_current.txt, results/shipped_example_external_postfix.txt, results/graph-reports/*.

refinement.detail: Searched, and found none this ticket should apply. The analyzer's standing recommendation remains to project [lastCommand, result], which no configured invariant reads; MF-028 and MF-029 both recorded strong arguments and still declined, and MF-030 adds no new evidence for or against it -- it changes how EXTENDS-decomposed models are scored, not what the binding model represents. MF-030's own finding is the opposite of a reduction: it reveals that the shipped decomposed example was previously UNDER-measured (External scored on 4 of 10 variables), so the honest movement here is toward MORE representation being counted, not less. The projection remains deferred to MF-023, where decomposition revisits it with per-component state spaces. Doctrine also bars a decrease independently while the three retention members are non-passing.

ticket.objective: CRITICAL -- the epic binding gate silently disables itself on the architecture SKILL.md mandates. analyze_complexity.py line 101 uses EXTENDS as a PARSE TERMINATOR, so a decomposed model is scored on only the declarations literally present in that file. MF-023 measured External reporting bound = 1 over 2 of 9 variables. THE ERROR IS NEVER CONSERVATIVE -- missing variables always shrink the bound, so the gate always fails TOWARD PASS. The shipped example has been scored this way for the whole epic. Resolve EXTENDS by following the module hierarchy and unioning declarations; report explicitly what is and is not handled (INSTANCE, substitution, LOCAL, parameterized instantiation) rather than implying full TLA+ module semantics. A partial resolver that DECLARES its limits and fails closed on constructs it cannot handle is acceptable; one that silently under-reports is not.
